Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We received a welcoming e-mail with guidance and then we should log on the university platform in a specific time slot on specific weekdays where it was possible to check in through a short meeting on Zoom.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail and guidance on Zoom.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy to register for classes and get the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get your learning agreement approved by the university as soon as possible and do it again as soon as possible if you change anything. Be aware that there sometimes are "internal rules" so they do not accept your enrollment in a course, but if you want the course then question these rules, since they are not always a final decree, if you can argue how the courses you want relate to your education.

questions.answer: I did mostly MA-courses but the level was allright even though I am doing a BA degree.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Italian Culture is a good way to learn about aspects of Italian history and culture that you were not expecting elsewhere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go visit other cities by train. Also go watch the local football games - you can get student tickets at the tourist office, or you can go to a local bar.

questions.answer: It was easy, very nice culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I do not recall challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Question if the university turns down your learning agreement with the reason of internal rules and no better explanation. Be aware of required physical participation in class, many courses have this as a criteria for passing. In the beginning I would recommend participating in all the classes you are interested in before choosing which courses you want to do and getting your learning agreement approved.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people, experiencing a new culture in depth and becoming more independent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the university system out. But I recommend going with the flow, feel your way and ask questions as soon as something is not well explained or does not seem fair.
